To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derived a new set of schizophrenia-specific factor scores and used these to perform gene pathway analyses that suggest that glutamatergics, GABA-A receptors, and cGMP may have differential influences on affective symptom expression in schizophrenia.

1) factor analysis of Operational Criteria Checklist items yielded 3 symptom factors, 2) these symptom factors were associated with specific genes and gene pathways, and 3), the findings suggest that glutamatergics, GABA-A receptors, and cyclic GAMP pathways may have differentially influence affective symptom presentation.
we have identified three SCZ-specific symptom dimensions that are associated with specific gene pathways and gene ontology terms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of gene pathways involved in the expression of specific symptom domains in schizophrenia.
the development of a schizophrenia-specific model of symptoms, based on factor analysis of Operational Criteria Checklist items, which can be used to derive phenotypes for gene-finding efforts.
identifying genes and gene pathways that may be involved in the expression of psychotic illness symptoms in schizophrenia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has demonstrated the feasibility of using a schizophrenia-only sample to derive factor scores for gene-based and gene pathway analyses of psychotic illness symptoms, and that these analyses have yielded some potentially novel findings.

the gene pathway analysis results are suggestive of involvement of the glutamatergicsynaptic transmission, GABAergic synapse, and cyclic GAMP pathways in the etiology of the manic symptom dimension in schizophrenia.
the results of these analyses are suggestive and require replication in independent samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study has identified a number of genes and pathways that may be important in the pathophysiology of psychotic symptoms in SCZ.
this study has provided a more refined set of symptom measures for gene pathway and genome-wide gene-based analysis of SCZ.
the use of a SCZ-specific symptom factor model, in a genome-wide gene pathway analysis, can yield novel insights into the genetic architecture of schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SCZ-specific symptom factors derived from this study are useful for gene-finding efforts.
the SCZ-specific factor scores are a useful phenotype for gene-finding efforts, and they may be particularly helpful for identifying genetic variants that modify SCZ symptoms.
the use of narrowly defined SCZ cases in factor analyses of symptoms may yield more sensitive phenotypic measures for gene-finding efforts.
